For more than a decade, neighbouring countries have been forced to endure the consequences of environmental negligence that disregards national borders, public health and regional well-being.

A coordinated regional response should hold those responsible accountable, pursue appropriate legal remedies and seek compensation for demonstrable economic losses, environmental damage and the devastating public-health consequences inflicted on neighbouring populations.

Indonesia cannot continue to treat a transboundary environmental crisis as though it were merely an internal domestic affair. Sovereignty is not a licence to pollute the air of neighbouring nations and economic interests must never be allowed to take precedence over human health and environmental responsibility.

Every year, the same old story! Indonesia burns forests, and Malaysia and other affected ASEAN countries get to enjoy the “free gift” of toxic haze! What a wonderful annual tradition!
Seriously, how many years must neighbouring countries suffer from the same problem? Instead of endless excuses, finger-pointing, and ego, how about taking real responsibility for once?
ASEAN countries affected by the haze should jointly summon Indonesia and demand a proper explanation. Enough is enough! ASEAN must take a much stricter stance and consider serious penalties against those responsible for repeatedly causing transboundary air pollution.
Why should Malaysia and other neighbouring countries suffer the consequences while those responsible get away with excuses? Is this what regional cooperation is supposed to look like?
If this problem keeps happening year after year, then clearly, stronger action is needed. ASEAN must stop relying on endless meetings and empty promises and start demanding measurable results, accountability, and effective prevention measures.
